act-2026-recovery.detail: Run the 2026 calendar recovery round across the whole portfolio — not a sample. Photograph every surviving 2026 gardien calendar so 2026 becomes full-year evidence instead of partial. The denominator is all active carbon points — the actively managed register less Marolinta, computed every build, and coverage achieved is to be reported against that denominator and no other. Prioritise the points with no dated 2026 sheet at all. The same round verifies that a calendar is physically present and legible at every point, which is a separate finding from whether it has been photographed — a point with no sheet on the wall needs a reissue, not a photograph. The round records the period at source, so attribution never depends on reading a printed header. Two steps, both before the shutter. First, the technician writes the year the sheet documents into the header, in pen — into the TAONA / ANNÉE box on v1.3 stock, or beside the pump identifier box on an older sheet — so the photograph itself carries the period. Second, the same year is entered as a field beside the photograph: a new whole-number question 2.15.7, “Année documentée par ce calendrier”, on the preventive-maintenance form de26d89a5c8a4452b42158c622be20d0, in question group d5233b2b immediately after 2.15.6, required whenever 2.15.6 carries an image. Where the year cannot be established from the sheet or from the gardien, the field is left empty and the period is treated as unproven — it is never filled in with the most likely year. Both steps are chapter 7 ter of the SOP. From the January round onward the period a sheet documents is recorded by the technician holding it, and is not inferred from the printed header. The question is live on the form as of 20 September 2026, id 3393e25651c047d0b8a29f34cdcf12d9, and is optional — stock already in the field carries no handwritten year, and a required field would force an invented answer. Making it required is a separate action below. The form carries French and English only, so the Malagasy wording — “Taona voarakitra amin’ity teti-andro ity” — leads the French label, as it does on the sheet itself; that too has its own action. Whole-portfolio, because the sampling question above is unsettled and the text leans against sampling the log; a sample would have to be redone if the answer is every point. Of carbon points, have no dated 2026 sheet at all. The tonnage and cash size of that gap is withdrawn with the per-year carbon basis it was computed from (act-carbon-year-basis) — the gap is those points, and it is evidence, not uplift: it protects the registered figure rather than exceeding it. A full-year 2026 record cannot be taken before 31 December 2026, by definition, so the round runs in January 2027. Field teams must be told immediately to leave the old sheet at the point when a new one is issued, and not to discard it. Replacement is rolling and continuous, so the evidence is at risk continuously rather than at a season. Feasibility is evidenced: sheets persist at points long after their year ends — 2024 sheets were still being photographed on 3 September 2026, twenty-one months later. Combine with the reissue round and the overdue preventive-maintenance round; the calendar is not a reason for a separate journey.

act-decommission-inactivity-field.detail: Decided 21 September 2026: SaniTap will not decommission or retire water points for inactivity. A pump that stays broken is a repair problem, not a register problem. It remains in the portfolio and is reported at its honest days operational. The reasoning is conservatism: removing under-performing points takes them out of the denominator and flatters the fleet average — the worst points leave the register and the reported availability of what remains rises, without a single pump working better. That is the less conservative treatment and the one a verifier would question. It is also what the methodology already assumes: neither version has any provision for a retired supply, because DOp,y is days operational and a pump that stops working simply contributes fewer of them. What follows: the 95% pause rule in the French suppression SOP is not applied and that SOP should be amended to say so; the permanent-deletion criteria are untouched, none of them being an availability judgement; no writable status property is needed in the register, because the only thing it was wanted for was a “paused” state that no longer exists, and the ZZ TEST name convention already handles the two records that are not water points; and repair speed becomes the only lever on days operational, which is why time to repair is now a headline metric above. Decision record, with the analysis that led to it: docs/decommissioning_rule_question.md. The original finding stands — the “jours d’inactivité” field exists on no live form — and is now moot for retirement, though the SOP amendment is not. Neither SOP is obsolete. Both carry permanent-deletion criteria that have nothing to do with availability — duplicate records, confirmed persistent contamination, irreparable or abandoned infrastructure, serious health or safety risk, a point taken over by another funder, no access — and all of those remain live. What is superseded is the 95% pause rule in the French SOP alone, which the English one never carried. That one clause should be struck; the documents stay.
